authority: CEO Round 156: 'Reproduce at least three public baseline approaches: physics-only, data-driven, physics+ML. Then compare C5-X. Do not declare the competitive white space empty until those baselines are actually characterized.'
constitutional_basis: Article IV — no fallback epistemology (cannot use weak baselines)
Article XIX — never optimize for the gate (baseline parameters frozen BEFORE C5-X runs)
Article XXVII — no threshold invention (AUROC + decision-benefit thresholds have provenance)
Article XXVIII — no silent semantic promotion (independent reproduction via clotFoam required)
Article XXIX — separate implementation from mechanism (baseline reproduction failure is implementation failure)
Article XXXII — state strongest alternative (academic groups may have undisclosed physics+ML approaches)

the_three_baselines.rule: C5-X must beat ALL THREE baselines. The competitive white space is NOT declared empty until all three are characterized.

baseline_A_physics_only.name: Physics-only thrombus fragmentation predictor
baseline_A_physics_only.description: Pure computational fluid dynamics + solid mechanics model of thrombus. Predicts fragmentation from stress/strain distribution. No learning component.
best_public_evidence: PMID 41663082 (2026 thrombosis digital twin review) — describes physics-only approaches
Bernsdorf et al., Thrombosis Research — CFD-thrombus work
Multiple CFD papers on thrombus stress analysis (2020-2025)
baseline_A_physics_only.epistemic_status: DEMONSTRATED in academic literature; no clinical product
baseline_A_physics_only.what_we_will_implement: Implement physics-only fragmentation predictor using our existing World A (FEBio 4.13), World D (CalculiX 2.23), and World E (SfePy 2026.2) infrastructure. Use published constitutive models for thrombus (hyperelastic + damage). Pre-register the constitutive parameters from literature.

physics_model.parameters: Pre-registered from published thrombus mechanical testing literature (e.g., Chueh et al. 2011, Tutino et al. 2017)
physics_model.failure_criterion: Maximum principal strain > epsilon_critical OR damage variable D > D_critical
physics_model.CFD_coupling: One-way coupling: flow → stress on thrombus surface; stress → fragmentation prediction

baseline_A_physics_only.fidelity_class: HIGH — we have working FEBio/CalculiX/SfePy from Round 131 three-way verification
baseline_A_physics_only.calibration_plan: Validate Baseline A against published benchmark cases (e.g., Chueh et al. thrombus stress distribution). If reproduction differs from published by >25%, baseline is INCOMPLETE (Article XXIX).

baseline_B_data_driven.name: Data-driven ML predictor (no physics)
baseline_B_data_driven.description: Pure ML predictor: features (clot geometry, flow conditions, patient history) → fragmentation risk. No physics simulation.
best_public_evidence: Image-based DL for clot histology (Tang et al. 2024-2025)
baseline_B_data_driven.epistemic_status: DEMONSTRATED in academic literature; no clinical product
baseline_B_data_driven.what_we_will_implement: Train gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost) + dense neural network (PyTorch) on simulated virtual cohort data. Features: clot geometry (length, cross-section, taper angle, volume), flow conditions (Reynolds number, wall shear stress, residence time), patient covariates. Target: binary fragmentation event. Cross-validate.

ml_architecture.model_1: XGBoost (gradient boosted trees) with hyperparameters pre-registered
ml_architecture.model_2: Dense NN (5 hidden layers, 64 units each, ReLU, dropout 0.3) with hyperparameters pre-registered
ml_architecture.training_data: 5000 simulated cases from virtual cohort (clot geometry × flow × patient covariates)

baseline_B_data_driven.fidelity_class: MEDIUM — we use standard ML libraries; specific architectures may differ from published
baseline_B_data_driven.calibration_plan: Compare Baseline B performance to published ML thrombus characterization benchmarks where available. If our Baseline B underperforms published by >25%, baseline is INCOMPLETE (Article XXIX).

baseline_C_physics_plus_ML.name: Physics + ML hybrid predictor
baseline_C_physics_plus_ML.description: Hybrid: physics simulation produces features (stress fields, fragmentation energy) → ML combines with patient features for prediction.
best_public_evidence: PMID 42508673 (2026 computational review) — describes multiple physics+ML approaches
Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for thrombosis (2023-2025 literature)
Reduced-order model + ML approaches for CFD acceleration (2023-2025)
baseline_C_physics_plus_ML.what_we_will_implement: Use our World A FEBio simulation to extract stress/strain features (max principal stress, strain energy density, damage variable), then train ML on (physics features + patient features) → fragmentation. This is the strongest plausible baseline.

hybrid_architecture.ml_model: XGBoost on (physics features + patient features) — same architecture as Baseline B but with additional physics features
hybrid_architecture.training_data: 5000 simulated cases from virtual cohort, with physics features extracted from FEBio simulation

baseline_C_physics_plus_ML.fidelity_class: HIGH for physics component (FEBio validated) + MEDIUM for ML component
baseline_C_physics_plus_ML.calibration_plan: Compare Baseline C performance to published physics+ML thrombus benchmarks where available.
baseline_C_physics_plus_ML.why_this_is_the_strongest_baseline: Baseline C combines the mechanistic strength of physics (Baseline A) with the predictive power of ML (Baseline B). If C5-X cannot beat this, the invention is not validated as better than the best publicly plausible approach.

the_three_baselines.alternative_explanation_to_state_explici: Multiple academic groups are pursuing similar physics+ML directions. Specific group implementations may be stronger than what we can reproduce from published methods. Article XXXII: state this alternative explicitly. If C5-X beats our reproduction of Baseline C, that is not the same as beating the strongest academic group's implementation.

experiment_design.pre_registration: This design is pre-registered BEFORE any C5-X code runs. Per Article XIX, no parameter may be tuned after C5-X results are known.

virtual_cohort.size: 500 virtual patients × 3 clot geometries × 3 flow conditions = 4500 cases
virtual_cohort.why_this_cohort: Stratification by clot geometry × flow × anatomy × material captures the major sources of thrombus fragmentation variability. C5-X must demonstrate advantage across the full space, not just average cases.

independent_reproduction_requirement.rule: C5-X prediction must survive actual clotFoam execution (OpenFOAM-9 external solver), not just our internal World C flow simulator.
independent_reproduction_requirement.why_required: Our World C is custom Python with internal formulas — NOT an independent solver. clotFoam is a widely-validated external CFD solver. If C5-X survives clotFoam, the prediction has independent physical reproduction (Article XXVIII). If it does not, the prediction is over-fit to our internal simulator.
independent_reproduction_requirement.implementation: Run C5-X prediction pipeline with World C as the flow simulator (training/primary). Then re-run with clotFoam as the flow simulator (independent verification). Compare predictions. If clotFoam predictions diverge from World C predictions by >20%, C5-X is KILLED for over-fitting (Article XXVIII).
independent_reproduction_requirement.openfoam_build_status: OpenFOAM-9 build was at 28% (1394/~4887 .o files) as of Round 155. Build must complete before C5-X-R1 can be executed.
independent_reproduction_requirement.build_dependency: C5-X-R1 is BLOCKED until OpenFOAM-9 build completes. This is a HARD dependency, not a soft one.

intervention_benefit_test.rule: Per CEO directive: 'The critical endpoint should ultimately be decision benefit, not AUROC alone. For example: reduced embolic-risk events under the same intervention budget.'
intervention_benefit_test.implementation: Simulate an intervention policy: max K interventions per N patients. Each predictor (Baseline A, B, C, C5-X) recommends which patients to intervene on. Compare: number of embolic-risk events prevented per intervention, under fixed budget K.
intervention_benefit_test.budget_levels: K = 10%, 25%, 50% of N (three budget levels tested)
intervention_benefit_test.rationale: AUROC alone is gameable: a predictor with high AUROC but poorly calibrated probabilities can lead to worse decisions under constrained budget. Decision benefit forces the predictor to be CALIBRATED, not just ranked.

primary_endpoint.mathematical_definition: Reduction in embolic-risk events (simulated) when an intervention policy is chosen using C5-X predictions vs intervention policy chosen using each baseline, under fixed intervention budget K.
primary_endpoint.why_this_endpoint: Per CEO directive: 'decision benefit, not AUROC alone'

secondary_endpoints: transfer_across_conditions (train on condition X, test on condition Y)
uncertainty_quantification_quality (predicted vs actual coverage of confidence intervals)

pre_registered_outcomes_table.outcome: WIN | KILL | INCONCLUSIVE per baseline × endpoint
rows: vs Baseline A on decision benefit
vs Baseline B (data-driven ML) on AUROC
vs Baseline B on decision benefit
vs Baseline C on decision benefit
independent reproduction via clotFoam (binary: SURVIVES / FAILS)
pre_registered_outcomes_table.decision_rule: C5-X is WIN only if ALL rows achieve WIN (or SURVIVES for the last row). C5-X is KILL if ANY row achieves KILL (or FAILS for the last row). Otherwise C5-X is INCONCLUSIVE.
pre_registered_outcomes_table.why_beat_all_three_baselines: Per CEO directive: 'Then C5-X must beat all three.' The moat is not established by beating one baseline — it is established by beating the strongest publicly plausible combination of physics, ML, and physics+ML approaches.

falsification_paths.rationale: Below 0.70, the predictor is not clinically actionable

falsification_paths.path: C5-X does not improve over best baseline by >= 0.05 AUROC → KILL
falsification_paths.rationale: Below 0.05 improvement is within typical cross-validation noise

falsification_paths.path: C5-X does not survive clotFoam (independent reproduction) → KILL
falsification_paths.evidence_required: World C predictions vs clotFoam predictions, divergence > 20%
falsification_paths.rationale: Article XXVIII — silent semantic promotion forbidden. A model that survives only in its training simulator is not validated.

falsification_paths.path: C5-X does not provide significant decision benefit over best baseline (p > 0.05) → KILL
falsification_paths.evidence_required: Decision benefit comparison at each budget level K
falsification_paths.rationale: If C5-X does not provide decision advantage, the invention is not useful

falsification_paths.path: Any of the three baselines (A, B, C) cannot be reproduced within 25% of published performance → BASELINE INCOMPLETE → experiment BLOCKED
falsification_paths.constitutional_basis: Article XXIX — separate implementation from mechanism. Baseline reproduction failure is NOT a C5-X failure.

falsification_paths.path: C5-X achieves 0.05-0.07 AUROC improvement over best baseline → INCONCLUSIVE
falsification_paths.next_step: Tighten experiment design OR public KILL with rationale (Article XXVIII)

adversarial_self_attack.attack_1_weak_baselines: An adversary would reproduce weak versions of each baseline to make C5-X look better. Counter: each baseline's parameters/architecture are pre-registered from literature; frozen BEFORE C5-X runs. Article XIX forbids post-hoc weakening.
adversarial_self_attack.attack_2_easy_cohort: An adversary would test on easy clot geometries (e.g., all cylindrical). Counter: cohort is stratified by geometry × flow × anatomy × material; C5-X must win across the full space.
adversarial_self_attack.attack_3_overfit_to_World_C: An adversary would train C5-X on World C outputs and test on World C outputs, claiming validation. Counter: independent reproduction via clotFoam is REQUIRED. Article XXVIII.
adversarial_self_attack.attack_4_AUROC_gaming: An adversary would report AUROC alone without decision benefit. Counter: BOTH AUROC and decision benefit must achieve WIN threshold.
adversarial_self_attack.attack_5_cherry_picked_budget: An adversary would cherry-pick the budget level K that makes C5-X look best. Counter: ALL THREE budget levels (10%, 25%, 50%) tested; C5-X must provide decision benefit at all three.
adversarial_self_attack.attack_6_silent_promotion: An adversary would silently promote 'beat our reproduction of Baseline C' to 'beat the strongest academic group's implementation'. Counter: explicit naming. Article XXVIII.

what_this_experiment_does_NOT_prove: Does NOT prove C5-X beats the strongest academic group's implementation of physics+ML — we reproduce from published methods, not from their code (Article XXXII)
Does NOT prove C5-X is clinically practical — virtual cohort only; real clinical validation required (Article XXXIV)
Does NOT prove C5-X works in vivo — virtual cohort uses simulated clots, not real patient thrombi

DOES prove: C5-X beats the strongest publicly plausible combination of physics + data-driven + physics+ML approaches, on a stratified virtual cohort, with independent reproduction via clotFoam, with decision benefit at multiple budget levels.
